title: Daily Life - How Would You Like Your Eggs
audio: mp3/69. Daily Life - How Would You Like Your Eggs.mp3

segments.zh: 你好英语学习者，欢迎回来。

segments.en: And today we're going to be bringing you a lesson about eggs.
segments.zh: 今天我们将为您带来有关鸡蛋的课程。

segments.en: And who knew there was so much to talk about when we're talking eggs.
segments.zh: 当我们谈论鸡蛋时，谁知道有很多话要说。

segments.en: Well, we always have eggs for breakfast and there are many ways of preparing them, so we're going to learn what the different ways are.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们早餐总是有鸡蛋，而且有很多准备方法，所以我们将了解不同的方法。

segments.en: Yes, and we'll learn some of the language that goes along with eggs.
segments.zh: 是的，我们将学习一些与鸡蛋一起使用的语言。

segments.en: So we have three words that we want to take a look at before we listen to our dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以在我们听对话之前，我们有三个词要看。

segments.en: So let's look at these in Vocabulary Preview.
segments.zh: 所以让我们在词汇预览中看看这些。

segments.en: Our preview word for this lesson is picky.
segments.zh: 我们本课的预览词很挑剔。

segments.en: So picky is an interesting adjective.
segments.zh: 所以picky是一个有趣的形容词。

segments.en: So if a person is picky, what does that mean?
segments.zh: 那么，如果一个人很挑剔，那是什么意思呢？

segments.en: So if your boss is picky and you give him a report and maybe it has, I don't know, a couple of mistakes or something.
segments.zh: 所以如果你的老板很挑剔，你给了他一份报告，我不知道，有几个错误或什么的。

segments.en: Yeah, he'll say, do it again.
So if you are picky, you want everything to be perfect.
segments.zh: 所以如果你很挑剔，你希望一切都是完美的。

segments.en: And if there's one small thing that's not, you won't be happy.
segments.zh: 如果有一件小事不是，你就不会高兴。
好的。 如此挑剔，有趣的词。
现在我们的下一个词，蛋黄。

segments.en: So this word is actually not in the dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以这个词实际上不在对话中。

segments.en: It's not in the dialogue, but it's important that you know, right?
segments.zh: 它不在对话中，但重要的是你知道，对吧？

segments.en: Okay. So if you have an egg, the yellow part is called the yolk.
segments.zh: 好的。 所以如果你有一个鸡蛋，黄色的部分叫做蛋黄。

segments.en: Okay. And what about the other part?
segments.zh: 好的。 而另一部分呢？

segments.en: Or also called the egg white, right?
Let's listen to our dialogue. We are going to be listening to a couple who are having breakfast.
segments.zh: 让我们听听我们的对话。 我们将听一对正在吃早餐的夫妇。

segments.en: Well, I felt like baking, so I made some muffins.
segments.zh: 我今天想烤点东西，就做了些松饼。

segments.en: Do you want me to make you some eggs?
I'll take mine sunny side up.
segments.zh: 我的要单面煎，蛋黄朝上。

segments.en: I don't know how you can eat your eggs like that.
segments.zh: 真不懂你怎么爱吃那样的煎蛋。

segments.en: Ever since I was small, I've had eggs and soldiers.
segments.zh: 我从小就爱吃半熟水煮蛋配吐司条。

segments.en: You know, my dad had scrambled eggs every morning for 20 years.
segments.zh: 我爸连续二十年每天早上都吃炒蛋。

segments.en: You know what really drives me crazy?
segments.zh: 你知道什么事最让我抓狂吗？

segments.en: When I ask for soft boiled eggs and they overcook them so they come out hard boiled.
segments.zh: 我点半熟水煮蛋，他们却煮过头，变成了全熟蛋。

segments.en: How can you dip your toast into a hard boiled egg?
segments.zh: 全熟蛋怎么拿吐司去蘸？

segments.en: Damn it. I said sunny side up.
segments.zh: 真是的，我说要单面煎、蛋黄朝上的！

segments.en: How many times do I have to tell you?
segments.zh: 我得说多少遍你才记得？

segments.en: So she is definitely very picky and has a very bad temper.
segments.zh: 所以她绝对很挑剔，脾气也很坏。

segments.en: I can't believe anyone would get so angry over their breakfast.
segments.zh: 我不敢相信有人会对他们的早餐如此生气。

segments.en: But I guess it is the most important meal of the day.
segments.zh: 但我想这是一天中最重要的一餐。

segments.en: Exactly. So we heard a couple of different ways of describing how you prepare eggs, so let's take a look at that in Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 没错。 所以我们听到了几种不同的方式来描述你如何准备鸡蛋，所以让我们在语言外卖中看看。

segments.en: Okay, so our first preparation method, my favorite, sunny side up.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们的第一个准备方法，我最喜欢的，阳光充足的一面朝上。
像太阳一样，阳光明媚，对吧？

segments.en: So when you fry an egg, right, and the yolk looks like a little sun, right?
segments.zh: 所以当你煎一个鸡蛋时，对，蛋黄看起来像一个小太阳，对吧？

segments.en: So why is it called sunny side up?
segments.zh: 那么为什么它被称为阳光面朝上呢？

segments.en: I think because of what you just said.
segments.zh: 我想是因为你刚才说的。

segments.en: But you don't cook the yolk, right?
Yeah, the yolk is still yellow.
It's still a little bit liquid. It's a little bit soft.
segments.zh: 它仍然有点液体。 它有点软。

segments.en: Okay, because the opposite would be a fried egg.
segments.zh: 好吧，因为相反的是煎蛋。

segments.en: So this, you put the egg in the pan and you cook it all the way through.
segments.zh: 所以这个，你把鸡蛋放在平底锅里，把它煮熟。

segments.en: So the yolk is not liquid anymore. It becomes hardened.
segments.zh: 所以蛋黄不再是液体了。 它变得坚硬。

segments.en: Let's take a look at our next set of eggs.
segments.zh: 让我们来看看我们的下一组鸡蛋。

segments.en: Okay, so to boil, you put the egg?
So how long would you usually put it in for to be soft boiled?
segments.zh: 那么你通常会把它放多久才能软煮？

segments.en: Three minutes, okay. So you only cook part of the egg, right?
segments.zh: 三分钟，好吧。 所以你只煮了一部分鸡蛋，对吧？

segments.en: The yolk, the yellow part, stays a little bit wet, a little bit liquid.
segments.zh: 蛋黄，黄色的部分，有点湿，有点液体。

segments.en: So again, the opposite would be?
segments.zh: 再说一次，相反的情况是？

segments.en: So hard boiled is when you cook the entire egg again.
segments.zh: 所以煮整个鸡蛋的时候，煮得很硬。

segments.en: Yes, so then it's hard like a ball.
segments.zh: 是的，所以它像球一样难。

segments.en: So with this soft boiled and hard boiled eggs, this takes us to our next form, eggs and soldiers.
segments.zh: 因此，有了这种煮熟和煮熟的鸡蛋，这将我们带到了我们的下一个形式，即鸡蛋和士兵。

segments.en: Now this is really interesting. I didn't really know about this before.
segments.zh: 现在这真的很有趣。 我以前真的不知道这件事。

segments.en: It kind of sounds like you're having eggs with a group of soldiers from the army.
segments.zh: 听起来你和一群军队的士兵一起吃鸡蛋。

segments.en: Well, this is a very British way of eating eggs. So you have your soft boiled egg in a cup and you have a piece of toast. But the toast is cut into long pieces.
segments.zh: 嗯，这是一种非常英国的吃鸡蛋的方式。 所以你把软煮鸡蛋放在杯子里，你有一块吐司。 但是吐司被切成长片。

segments.en: And then you take those pieces and you dip them into the egg yolk.
segments.zh: 然后你把这些碎片浸入蛋黄中。

segments.en: Yeah. Typical English way of eating eggs.
segments.zh: 是的。 典型的英国吃鸡蛋的方式。

segments.en: So eggs and soldiers. Interesting. And this takes us to our last form of egg preparation and probably the most popular.
segments.zh: 所以鸡蛋和士兵。 有趣。 这将我们带到了最后一种形式的鸡蛋制备，可能是最受欢迎的。

segments.en: Take eggs, put them in a pan and then you just move them all over the place.
segments.zh: 取鸡蛋，把它们放在平底锅里，然后把它们移动到整个地方。

segments.en: So the yolk and the white are mixed together.
segments.zh: 所以蛋黄和白色混合在一起。

segments.en: So we've looked at a lot of egg preparation and now we can listen to our dialogue for the second time and then we'll come back and look at some phrases.
segments.zh: 所以我们看了很多鸡蛋准备，现在我们可以第二次听我们的对话，然后我们会回来看一些短语。

segments.en: Well, I felt like baking so I made some muffins.
segments.zh: 嗯，我想烘焙，所以我做了一些松饼。

segments.en: Do you want me to make you some eggs?
I'll take mine sunny side up.
segments.zh: 我会把我的阳光一面朝上。

segments.en: I don't know how you can eat your eggs like that.
segments.zh: 真不懂你怎么爱吃那样的煎蛋。

segments.en: Ever since I was small, I've had eggs and soldiers.
segments.zh: 自从我很小，我就有了鸡蛋和士兵。

segments.en: You know, my dad had scrambled eggs every morning for 20 years.
segments.zh: 我爸连续二十年每天早上都吃炒蛋。

segments.en: You know what really drives me crazy?
segments.zh: 你知道什么事最让我抓狂吗？

segments.en: When I asked for soft boiled eggs and they overcook them so they come out hard boiled.
segments.zh: 当我要软煮鸡蛋时，他们把它们煮过头，所以它们煮熟了。

segments.en: How can you dip your toast into a hard boiled egg?
segments.zh: 全熟蛋怎么拿吐司去蘸？

segments.en: How many times do I have to tell you?
segments.zh: 我得说多少遍你才记得？

segments.en: Interesting that the man in this dialogue is the one doing the baking.
segments.zh: 有趣的是，这个对话中的人是做烘焙的人。

segments.en: Well, that's modern days. I don't know. Men are learning how to cook and yeah.
segments.zh: 嗯，这就是现代。 我不知道。 男人正在学习如何做饭，是的。

segments.en: All right. Well, since this house husband felt like baking, I think we should look at this and one other phrase in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 好的。 好吧，既然这位家庭丈夫想烘焙，我想我们应该看看 Fluency Builder 中的另一个短语。

segments.en: He said, I felt like baking.
So let's take a look at this.
segments.zh: 所以让我们来看看这个。

segments.en: He feels like or he felt like in the past.
segments.zh: 他觉得或他感觉像过去一样。

segments.en: What does that mean when you feel like?
segments.zh: 当你喜欢的时候，这意味着什么？

segments.en: You have the desire to do it.
And now this verb is in the gerund form.
segments.zh: 现在这个动词是动名词形式。

segments.en: Right. I feel like eating lunch.
I felt like going to the movies.
That's the way you would say this.
segments.zh: 这就是你会这么说的方式。

segments.en: And now let's take a look at this second phrase.
segments.zh: 现在让我们来看看第二个短语。

segments.en: This is a very, very descriptive phrase.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常非常描述性的短语。

segments.en: And I think if we listen to some examples, it will help us understand the meaning.
segments.zh: 我想如果我们听一些例子，它会帮助我们理解它的含义。

segments.en: This music is driving me crazy.
Don't leave garbage in my car.
segments.zh: 不要把垃圾留在我的车里。

segments.en: Your mom is driving me crazy.
So if something drives you crazy.
segments.zh: 所以如果有什么东西让你发疯。

segments.en: It makes you feel very angry or annoyed.
segments.zh: 它让你感到非常生气或恼火。

segments.en: But it can also be positive, right? Like that girl drives me crazy.
segments.zh: 但它也可以是积极的，对吧？ 就像那个女孩让我发疯。

segments.en: As in you really, really, really like her.
segments.zh: 就像你真的，真的，真的很喜欢她。

segments.en: I don't know. It sounds a little bit inappropriate to me.
segments.zh: 我不知道。 这对我来说听起来有点不合适。

segments.en: Like she's got me thinking and she's got me in the clouds or something like that.
segments.zh: 就像她让我思考，她让我在云端或类似的东西中。

segments.en: Well, maybe there's something about you that I don't need to know.
segments.zh: 好吧，也许你有什么我不需要知道的。

segments.en: So I'll just let you keep that thought to yourself.
segments.zh: 所以我会让你把这个想法留给自己。

segments.en: Well, I'm just saying we could use it in a positive form as well.
segments.zh: 好吧，我只是说我们也可以以积极的形式使用它。

segments.en: So drives me crazy. Really great phrase.
segments.zh: 所以让我发疯。 真的很棒的短语。

segments.en: And you can use it in all of these different situations like we heard.
segments.zh: 您可以像我们听到的那样在所有这些不同的情况下使用它。

segments.en: So let's listen to our dialogue for the last time and then we'll come back and talk a little bit more.
segments.zh: 所以让我们最后一次听我们的对话，然后我们会回来多谈谈。

segments.en: Well, I felt like baking so I made some muffins.
segments.zh: 嗯，我想烘焙，所以我做了一些松饼。

segments.en: Do you want me to make you some eggs?
I'll take mine sunny side up.
segments.zh: 我会把我的阳光一面朝上。

segments.en: I don't know how you can eat your eggs like that.
segments.zh: 真不懂你怎么爱吃那样的煎蛋。

segments.en: Ever since I was small, I've had eggs and soldiers.
segments.zh: 自从我很小，我就有了鸡蛋和士兵。

segments.en: You know, my dad had scrambled eggs every morning for 20 years.
segments.zh: 我爸连续二十年每天早上都吃炒蛋。

segments.en: You know what really drives me crazy?
segments.zh: 你知道什么事最让我抓狂吗？

segments.en: When I ask for soft boiled eggs and they overcook them so they come out hard boiled.
segments.zh: 我点半熟水煮蛋，他们却煮过头，变成了全熟蛋。

segments.en: How can you dip your toast into a hard boiled egg?
segments.zh: 全熟蛋怎么拿吐司去蘸？

segments.en: Damn it. I said sunny side up.
segments.zh: 该死的。 我说阳光一面朝上。

segments.en: How many times do I have to tell you?
segments.zh: 我得说多少遍你才记得？

segments.en: Well, I think there are some people who really, really love eating eggs for breakfast and some people who just can't stand it.
segments.zh: 好吧，我认为有些人真的非常喜欢早餐吃鸡蛋，有些人无法忍受。

segments.en: I mean, who doesn't like eggs in the morning?
segments.zh: 我的意思是，早上谁不喜欢鸡蛋？
对吗？ 鸡蛋，培根，吐司。

segments.en: Now you were telling me that you have some traditions when you eat eggs.
segments.zh: 现在你告诉我，当你吃鸡蛋时，你有一些传统。

segments.en: I think, I'm not sure if this is just in my family, but I think actually it might be common with other people as well.
segments.zh: 我想，我不确定这是否只是我的家人，但我认为实际上它也可能与其他人很常见。

segments.en: When you eat a soft boiled or hard boiled egg, you have to eat all of the egg outside of the shell and then you have to break the bottom of the shell after you finished.
segments.zh: 当你吃一个煮熟或煮熟的鸡蛋时，你必须把所有的鸡蛋都吃掉，然后你必须在完成后打破壳的底部。

segments.en: So that the fairies who live in your egg cup can come out.
segments.zh: 这样住在你蛋杯里的仙女们就可以出来了。

segments.en: So it's kind of like a superstition.

segments.zh: 是的。 所以我不知道。

segments.en: You guys, do you have any egg traditions or any other crazy food stories like that?
segments.zh: 你们，你们有鸡蛋传统或任何其他疯狂的美食故事吗？

segments.en: Well, for example, I was telling you that when I prepare scrambled eggs, sometimes I like to take some rice, some rice that has already been cooked, put it in the pan and then take some eggs, two eggs, put it on top of the rice and scramble the rice with the eggs.
segments.zh: 好吧，例如，我告诉你，当我准备炒鸡蛋时，有时我喜欢吃一些米饭，一些已经煮熟的米饭，把它放在锅里，然后拿一些鸡蛋，两个鸡蛋，放在米饭上，用鸡蛋炒米饭。

segments.en: Yeah, it could be for breakfast.
Yeah. A little bit. Not like a huge plate of rice or maybe at night you don't have anything to eat.
segments.zh: 是的。 一点点。 不像一大盘米饭，或者在晚上你没有东西吃。

segments.en: Well, it's also a quick man's food.
segments.zh: 嗯，它也是一个快速的男人的食物。

segments.en: So let us know if you guys have any egg preparations or any special egg recipes or traditions that you practice.
segments.zh: 因此，如果你们有任何鸡蛋制剂或任何特殊的鸡蛋食谱或您练习的传统，请告诉我们。

segments.en: Visit our website at EnglishPod.com where you can leave all of your comments and questions.
segments.zh: 访问我们的网站 englishpod.com，您可以在其中留下您的所有评论和问题。

segments.en: And as always, we are there to answer them and solve any problems.
segments.zh: 与往常一样，我们在那里回答并解决任何问题。

segments.en: Well, we're out of time for today, but until next time, bye.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们今天没有时间了，但直到下一次，再见。
